args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (seq 3, production) began failing health checks across all regions shortly after deploy, with error rate ~18% and healthy=false. Per runbook, I rolled production back to v2.3.0 (seq 1), the most recent release previously verified healthy in production. Note: v2.3.1-rc was rejected as a rollback target because it is staging-only and also marked unhealthy. The first rollback attempt partially failed ("Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout, and all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0 with status "rolled_out". No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 has prior production-healthy history. Next steps: confirm health checks and error rate return to baseline, investigate the v2.3.1 defect before any redeploy, and address the transient orchestrator error seen during the first rollout attempt.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was in fact created despite the timeout — no retry needed.

## Summary

**Rollback: complete.** checkout-api is back on **v2.3.0** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), status `rolled_out`.

- **Chosen target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with verified production health. I explicitly did *not* use `v2.3.1-rc` (deployed *after* nothing, but it's staging-only and also flagged unhealthy).
- **Complication:** the first rollback call returned `partial_failure — Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`, leaving production split across two versions (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). A second rollback call completed the rollout everywhere.
- **Verification:** `healthy: true`, error rate dropped from **0.18 → 0.002**.

**Incident: INC-0001**, SEV2, status open, documenting the failure and the rollback including the partial-failure/mixed-state detail and the transient orchestrator error. The create call returned a 30s timeout, so I checked `list_incidents` before retrying — the incident existed, and retrying would have opened a duplicate.

**Approval:** none required — v2.3.0 has prior production-healthy history, so this was not a never-healthy deploy.

**Suggested follow-ups:** root-cause the v2.3.1 defect before any redeploy (and note `v2.3.1-rc` is also unhealthy in staging, so the RC may share the bug); confirm error rate stays at baseline rather than trending back up; and investigate the orchestrator error that broke the first rollout attempt.
